statement: To legally change your name in Rhode Island, you petition the probate court in the town or city where you live. Rhode Island law says a name change must be granted unless it is sought for a fraudulent purpose, and the court may not require you to publish public notice of the change before approving it.
detail: If you are indigent or show a limited ability to pay, the court may waive or reduce the court costs. The court may also require you to undergo a criminal history record check as part of the petition.

cost.note: The statute doesn't set a specific filing-fee amount, though it allows the court to waive or reduce court costs for a petitioner who is indigent or has a limited ability to pay. Contact the probate court where you're filing for the current fee.
cost.fee_waiver_criteria: If a petitioner is indigent, or demonstrates a limited or inability to pay, the court costs may be waived or reduced.

source.title: Rhode Island General Laws § 33-22-28 — Name Change

topic: Rhode Island driver's license name change
statement: To change the name on your Rhode Island driver's license or ID, you bring your current license to any DMV branch location (or an AAA branch office if you're a member) and complete the License/ID/Permit Application (LI-1 Form) along with one document showing your correct name. You must update your name with Social Security first — it takes 24 hours for a Social Security change to become effective before the DMV can process your transaction.
detail: The costs for this transaction are listed in the DMV's own Fee Table.

cost.note: The page doesn't state a dollar amount directly — it points to the DMV's own Fee Table. Contact the DMV for the current fee.

source.title: Rhode Island DMV — Name & Address Change

topic: Rhode Island driver's license gender designation
statement: To change the gender designation on your Rhode Island driver's license or ID, you surrender your current state-issued license or ID, submit a completed Gender Designation form, pay the applicable fee for a new or updated card, and have a new photograph taken. DMV employees may not ask for gender-related information beyond what the form itself requires, or ask about your private medical history or records.
detail: Changing the name that goes with a gender change is done separately, through appropriate court documents, and must also be reflected on your Social Security card. The DMV's own Gender Designation form is covered in a companion record — read it for what the form itself asks.

cost.note: The page doesn't state a dollar amount for this transaction — it points to the DMV's own Fee Table. Contact the DMV for the current fee.

source.title: Rhode Island DMV — Name & Address Change

topic: Rhode Island DMV Gender Designation form
statement: Rhode Island DMV's Gender Designation form ("Gender Designation on a License or Identification Card") asks you to check the designation you want your driver's license or ID card to read: M, F, or X. You declare under penalty of perjury that the statements on the application are true and complete.
detail: The form restates the DMV's procedure: surrender any current state-issued license or ID card, submit the completed form, pay the applicable fees for a new or updated card, and have a new photograph taken. It says DMV employees shall not request additional gender-related information beyond what the form requires or ask about your private medical history or records, and that the form contains private medical information kept confidential under the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act. Name changes related to gender are done through court documents and must also be reflected on your Social Security card. The form is marked rev. 7/20.

cost.note: The form says to pay the applicable fees for a new or updated license or ID card without stating an amount. Contact the DMV for the current fee.

source.title: Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles — Gender Designation on a License or Identification Card (form, rev. 7/20)

topic: Rhode Island birth certificate name change
statement: Rhode Island's vital-records rule lets you amend the given name on a birth certificate with an affidavit from the registrant (if of legal age) or their parent, guardian, or legal representative, plus one evidentiary document. But once more than 30 days have passed since the birth was registered, a change that reflects a genuinely new given name — rather than a spelling fix or clerical correction — can only be made after you submit a court order directing it.
detail: This is the same evidentiary-documentation rule the State Registrar applies to any correction of a vital record: an affidavit plus at least one original supporting document (or a certified copy) established within seven years of the fact it supports. If the Registrar finds the evidence unsatisfactory, the record will not be amended unless a court of competent jurisdiction orders it.

source.title: Rhode Island Code of Regulations 216-RICR-10-10-1 § 1.37 — Requirements to Amend Vital Records

topic: Rhode Island birth certificate sex designation
statement: To correct the sex shown on a Rhode Island birth certificate so it differs from the sex on the original record, Rhode Island's vital-records rule requires only an affidavit — executed by you if you're of legal age, or by your parent, legal guardian, or legal representative if you're not. The State Registrar then changes the certificate to reflect the new sex designation without indicating that a change was made.
detail: If your correction request for sex also includes a request for a legal name change, the certificate will be marked "Amended" only with respect to the name change — the sex correction itself leaves no such mark. The rule describes no separate requirement for a court order or a physician's statement to change the sex marker alone. The Department of Health's own requirements sheet and its web page add procedural steps the rule itself doesn't spell out — read the companion records before you go.

source.title: Rhode Island Code of Regulations 216-RICR-10-10-1 § 1.37 — Requirements to Amend Vital Records

topic: Rhode Island birth certificate sex-field change: RIDOH's requirements
statement: The Rhode Island Department of Health's own requirements sheet says that, since October 1, 2019, the sex field on a Rhode Island birth certificate can be changed to reflect your sex or gender identity. The person whose certificate will change must come to the Office of Vital Records in person to self-attest, so staff can create an affidavit for that person to sign; if the person is younger than 18, their parent, legal guardian, or legal representative signs it. The sheet says people can change the sex field from M to F or F to M using the affidavit, and that people born in Rhode Island who identify as non-binary or neither male nor female can change it to X.
detail: Bring a government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, Certificate of Naturalization, or Alien Registration Card). People of any age can make this change, but minors need parental or guardian consent. The sheet also says that once an item has been amended on a vital record it cannot be changed again unless the State Registrar receives a court order. This is the department's procedural guidance; the underlying vital-records rule is covered in a companion record.

cost.note: The $10 is to make the change on the birth record. A copy of the changed record costs $22 for in-person customers or $25 by mail.

source.title: Rhode Island Department of Health, Office of Vital Records — Requirements and Fees for Changes to Birth, Marriage, or Death Records

topic: Rhode Island birth certificate amendment: who can request, ID, and processing time
statement: The Rhode Island Department of Health says it takes 3 - 4 weeks to process an amendment request for a birth, death, or marriage record. To make a change you must provide a valid, government-issued photo identification to prove you are entitled to make the request — a driver's license, passport, military identification, Certificate of Naturalization, or Alien Registration Card — and if you request the change by mail you must include a readable copy of one of those.
detail: Vital records are confidential, so changes can only be requested by you; your mother, father, child, sibling, guardian, or authorized agent; attorneys, title examiners, or members of legally incorporated genealogical societies conducting official duties; a person who needs the information to determine or protect personal or property rights; or a person with a court order instructing the registrar to change the document. The Center of Vital Records is at 6 Harrington Rd., Cranston, and the page says an appointment is suggested. For the requirements specific to a name change or sex change, the page points to the department's own requirements document, covered in companion records.

timeline.typical: 3 - 4 weeks to process an amendment request

source.title: Rhode Island Department of Health — Changes To Birth, Death Or Marriage Records

topic: Rhode Island birth certificate amendment fees
statement: Rhode Island's fee schedule for the Department of Health lists $10.00 for an authorized correction, alteration, or addition to a vital record, and $22.00 for a certified copy of a vital record.
detail: Each duplicate certified copy ordered at the same time costs $18.00, and expedited service adds a $7.00 handling fee to the basic fee.

cost.note: A certified copy of the amended birth certificate costs $22.00 more; each additional duplicate ordered at the same time costs $18.00.

source.title: Rhode Island Code of Regulations 216-RICR-10-05-2 § 2.17 — Vital Records Fees
